LuDingDasgupta2018 constructs fixed-marginal ordinal couplings, but not endpoint-preserving completions to an IV law with treatment-induced selection.
GabrielSachsJensen2024 reports symbolic/computational ordinal bounds in noncompliance settings; the claimed general threshold-flow implementation would be a useful but supporting algorithmic advance.

FangSantos2019, ChernozhukovLeeRosen2013, Semenova2025, and deAguasEtAl2025 do not establish the stated simultaneous uniform coverage result for this composed two-endpoint map.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 3 (three-level witness)
soundness_flags.one_line: The witness specifies only capacities, not an observed law or a quantified compatible-law class, so its use of Θ_I(P_obs) and its claimed full-law attainment are not yet well-defined.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 5 and def:plugin-endpoint-estimator
soundness_flags.one_line: “Project … onto the finite-dimensional cone” does not specify a projection metric or optimization rule, leaving Ψ̂_n and hence its asserted directional derivative undefined.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper imposes conditional IV assumptions and weak selection monotonicity for compliers, allows its direction to vary with covariates, and identifies selected-complier masses for mean-effect bounds.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv v3, 5 April 2018, author version corresponding to the cited 2018 journal article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The source gives sharp lower and upper bounds for the strict-benefit probability from fixed ordinal potential-outcome marginals and states constructive attainability.

The source gives probability-of-benefit bounds under confounding and under an IV/noncompliance DAG, with no-defiers results for finite ordinal supports; its estimand is full-population rather than survivor-complier benefit under selection.
The paper studies probability of tiered benefit for ordered outcomes, gives sharp bounds under its causal assumptions, and addresses nonregular inference from individualized optimization ambiguities.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the capacity-only three-level witness by a complete one-cell observed-data table (including p_x and instrument probabilities), or quantify the proposition over every compatible observed law with the displayed capacities.

Define the capacity-cone projection as a specified Euclidean projection or explicit strictly convex quadratic program, including its cell-screening normalization, before asserting the pointwise derivative.

Sharpen the uniform-inference handle into an explicit multiplier critical-value construction with stated rates for a_n and η_n, then prove coverage first on a fixed finite-cell face before allowing changing support.

recommended_next_step: Revise the witness and plug-in estimator definitions, then return the unchanged sharp partial-transport kernel for Stage 0.
